item.title: Swatch beats Samsung in court: 11.6 million in compensation
item.description: Swatch wins in London against Samsung: the court orders the giant to pay $11.6 million for counterfeiting digital dials.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief
- Swatch wins lawsuit in London against Samsung: $11.6 million in damages - Samsung copied digital watch faces with logos of 10 Swiss brands - Approximately 160,000 illegal downloads in the UK and EU between 2015 and 2019
## Key Facts
- **What**: Counterfeit digital watch faces on Galaxy App Store - Where: London Court - Who: Swatch Group vs Samsung Electronics - When: Violations from 2015 to 2019 - Amount: $11.6 million (vs. $170 million requested) - Brands: Breguet, Blancpain, Jaquet Droz, Glashütte Original, Omega, Longines, Tissot, Hamilton, Mido, Swatch - Users: Approximately 160,000 downloads
Swatch has won a significant victory in a case judged by a British court against South Korean tech giant Samsung. The London court has sentenced Samsung Electronics to pay $11.6 million to the Swiss watch company for trademark infringement. The ruling comes after years of litigation on a specific issue: the digital counterfeiting of watch faces.
The story concerns applications that can be downloaded from Samsung's Galaxy App Store platform, available between October 2015 and February 2019. These apps offered watch faces that mimicked protected designs from ten brands of the Swatch Group: Breguet, Blancpain, Jaquet Droz, Glashütte Original, Omega, Longines, Tissot, Hamilton, Mido and Swatch itself. The apps were available both for free and for a fee and recorded around 160,000 downloads in the UK and European Union.
### The incredible gap: from $301 to $11.6 million
What is surprising about the ruling is the enormous distance between the negotiating positions. Samsung Electronics, in fact, was initially willing to pay only $301 to the other party as compensation. Swatch Group, on the other hand, had claimed $170 million for the systematic infringement of trademarks. The British court found a middle ground: $11.6 million. Although it is a fraction of the amount requested by Swatch, the ruling represents a substantial recognition of the damage caused by counterfeiting and the massive spread of fraudulent applications in two important markets: the United Kingdom and the EU.
The lawsuit covered a specific period, from 2015 to 2019, during which counterfeit apps circulated on Samsung's platform without permission. The fact that Samsung was willing to offer less than $300 initially suggests that the tech company knowingly underestimated the reputational and economic damage done to the Swatch Group's luxury brands. The $11.6 million award represents a tangible economic achievement for the Swatch Group in the current business environment. The Swiss company, which is listed on the Zurich stock exchange, has recovered in recent years after a difficult period in the watch industry. A favorable ruling on intellectual property helps to strengthen trademark protection in the global market and sends an important signal to competitors about the cost of counterfeiting.
The proliferation of counterfeit apps on app stores is a growing phenomenon in the digital economy. Unlike counterfeiting physical products, which requires manufacturing infrastructure, digital counterfeiting is facilitated by scalability and the difficulty in controlling millions of applications available on the platforms. In Samsung's case, the 160,000 downloads recorded in the UK and EU highlight the scale of the problem: a significant user base that has come into contact with fake versions of Swatch products.
### The precedent in digital markets
The British court's ruling underlines the importance of local jurisdiction in protecting intellectual property rights. The UK and the EU have some of the strictest standards of protection in the world. This factor has presumably favored Swatch's position in legal negotiation. In addition, the court was able to assess the actual damage in terms of users reached, downloads, potential loss of sales, and reputational damage to the brand.
Swatch's victory not only affects Breguet, Blancpain, Omega, Longines, Tissot, Hamilton and Mido — the partner brands of the Swatch Group — but also the entire Swiss watch industry. Luxury watches represent a product category where design, heritage and brand are fundamental elements of commercial value. Counterfeiting, even in digital form, erodes these intangible elements that Swiss manufacturers have developed and invested in over decades.
### Implications for the Swiss watch industry
The decision sets an important legal precedent: international courts are willing to recognize the damage from digital counterfeiting and award proportionate compensation. This can encourage other Swiss luxury manufacturers to legally protect themselves against similar infringements in other channels, from app stores to social networks, from online marketplaces to e-commerce sites. The message is clear: intellectual property is also protected in digital form and infringements have significant economic consequences. [Scopri di più sulle aziende svizzere che operano nel settore del lusso](nav:companies) to understand the economic weight of this segment in the national economy.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare [CHF-EUR exchange options](nav:exchange) and [banks for cross-border workers](nav:banks). If you're a Swiss consumer interested in technology and watches, the London ruling offers an important practical lesson: the reliability of the source from which you download apps. Counterfeit apps that mimicked Swatch, Omega, Longines, and other brands were available on Samsung's Galaxy App Store, an official platform. This means that even app stores run by big tech manufacturers require careful user verification.
### How to recognize counterfeit apps
The first defense is to verify the developer's name. Legitimate apps from Swatch, Omega, and other luxury brands are published directly by the proprietary companies or clearly identifiable authorized partners. If an app offers popular design watch faces but is not published by the official company, it is almost certainly counterfeit.
Second, look at reviews and the total number of downloads. Official apps from established brands have thousands or hundreds of thousands of downloads with a pattern of verified reviews. Counterfeit apps, even if they are mass-downloaded as in the Samsung case, often have a less professional profile.
Finally, consider the price and features. A legitimate watch face from a luxury brand generally costs between $0.99 and $4.99. If you find deals that are too affordable or apps that promise access to premium content without in-app purchases, be wary.
### What to do if you downloaded a counterfeit app
If you were exposed to counterfeit apps from the Galaxy App Store between 2015 and 2019, there's no immediate risk to your device — it wasn't malware. You simply used an unauthorized product that infringed on the Swatch Group's trademark. You can uninstall the app if you want. Samsung removed all unauthorized apps from its platform after the end of the availability period (February 2019), so exposure to the issue is now historic.
For the future, remember to download phone customization apps (such as smartwatch faces) only from official stores and verified brand profiles. Apple App Store, Google Play Store and Samsung Galaxy App Store have improved control systems compared to the years 2015-2019, but it always remains a shared responsibility between the platform and the end user.
If you are interested in the topic of intellectual property — especially in the context of luxury and Swiss technology — you can learn more about how trademark rights work in the global market. The Swatch Group remains one of the world's largest players in the watch industry and represents excellence in Swiss engineering and design globally. The London ruling shows that intellectual property rights are also protected in digital form and that international courts are willing to sanction substantial infringements with significant compensation. item.title: 2025 parties: 24.6 million, -1 million from 2024
item.description: In 2025, Swiss parties declare 24.6 million francs of revenue, a decrease of about one million compared to 2024. The SP leads with 7.9 million francs.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - 24.6 million: total funding declared by the 9 parties in 2025 - Decrease of ~1 million compared to 2024 (they were 25.6 million) - PS leads with 7.9 million, FDP second with 4.8 million
## Key Facts - **What**: Annual Declaration of Funding of Swiss Federal Political Parties - Who: Swiss Federal Audit Office (SFAO) - When: 2025 (data published by the SFAO) - Where: Switzerland (9 of 10 parties in the Federal Assembly) - Total amount: CHF 24.6 million - Change: -1 million compared to 2024 (3.9% decrease)
The Swiss Federal Audit Office (SFAO) has published data on the revenue reported by political parties for 2025. Nine of the ten parties represented in the Federal Assembly recorded total revenues of CHF 24.6 million, around one million less than in the previous year, when total revenues amounted to CHF 25.6 million. The declarations are made on the basis of the rules on the transparency of the financing of Swiss politics.
The Socialist Party (SP) remains the first in terms of fundraising capacity, with revenues of CHF 7.9 million. It is followed by the Radical Liberal Party (FDP) with CHF 4.8 million, the Swiss People's Party (SVP) with CHF 3.8 million and the Centre Party with CHF 2.7 million. These four parties have representatives in the Federal Council, Switzerland's executive chamber.
Among the four government parties, the SP and the FDP recorded a decrease in revenue compared to 2024, by CHF 0.3 million and CHF 1.8 million, respectively. The People's Party and the Centre, on the other hand, recorded an increase in revenue, by CHF 1 million and CHF 0.1 million, respectively.
### The other parties
Among the smaller parties, the Greens declared revenues of 1.8 million francs, while the liberal Greens reached 1.2 million. Revenues of less than one million francs were declared by the Federal Democratic Union (UDF), the Evangelical Party (ENP) and the Mouvement Citoyens Genevois (MCG). The Lega dei Ticinese, the only party among the ten represented in the Federal Assembly, has not yet disclosed its funding for 2025, representing the only gap in the annual transparency landscape. The overall decline of around one million francs compared to 2024 highlights a downward trend in fundraising in the Swiss political landscape. This figure, despite its apparent numerical modesty (a decline of 3.9% year-on-year), reflects deeper dynamics in Swiss politics and the ability of parties to attract resources from private donors and supporters.
### Internal redistribution
Looking at the internal movements between the main government parties, a mixed picture emerges. While the SP and FDP suffered repercussions in 2025 (-0.3 and -1.8 million respectively), the SVP compensated with a growth of 1 million and the Centre maintained stability with a minimal increase of 0.1 million. The largest relative loss belongs to the FDP, which recorded a 27% drop from its 2024 revenue, suggesting a possible rearrangement of the donor base between centre-right forces.
At the same time, the overall decline did not evenly affect all parties. The Greens maintained a substantial collection (1.8 million), while the liberal Greens remain at 1.2 million. This segmentation of the party landscape shows that the volatility of funding is uneven, with some parties maintaining a stable donor base and others suffering from greater variability.
### Transparency and democratic accountability
The annual declarations published by the SFAO are a pillar of Swiss democratic transparency. They allow citizens to understand how the parties finance themselves and, indirectly, what the economic influence of the various stakeholders is in the Swiss political landscape. The fact that one of the ten parties (Lega dei Ticinese) has not yet provided data for 2025 underlines the importance of systematic monitoring of this information and compliance with federal transparency regulations.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare [CHF-EUR exchange options](nav:exchange) and [banks for cross-border workers](nav:banks). ### Where to find the data and how to access it
Data on party-reported funding is publicly available thanks to transparency regulations on political financing. The Swiss Federal Audit Office (SFAO) publishes this information annually, allowing anyone to verify the revenues declared by each party. Accessing this data does not require complex procedures: it is sufficient to consult the SFAO's annual reports, available through the official website of the Swiss federal administration.
For citizens interested in understanding the Swiss political landscape and the fundraising capacity of the various parties, this data represents an essential tool. Knowing the funding sources and declared amounts helps form an informed opinion on any economic influences within the national political system.
### Future scenarios and monitoring
The decline recorded in 2025 could be temporary or signal a structural shift in donor generosity toward the Swiss political system. In the coming years, it will be interesting to observe whether the downward trend continues or stabilizes. The annual publication of data by the SFAO ensures that every citizen can follow this trend, contributing to an informed public debate on the country's economic-political dynamics.
Swiss national politics, financed by private revenues, directly influences the economic well-being of residents. From decisions on the [cost of living](nav:cost-of-living) to taxes and the labour market, everything traces back to the political priorities set by the parties and their funders.

item.title: Sick pay premiums Freiburg: reduction and subsidies
item.description: Guide to compulsory health insurance premiums in the Canton of Fribourg: deductibles, alternative models and procedure for obtaining premium reductions
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Health insurance LAMal is mandatory in Switzerland and also valid in Fribourg - Available deductibles range from CHF 300 to CHF 2500 for adults - The Canton of Fribourg offers subsidies (premium reduction) for residents with low income - The registration procedure must take place within 3 months of arrival in Switzerland
## Key facts - **What**: Mandatory health insurance with per capita premiums and variable deductibles - Where: Canton of Fribourg (national LAMal system applied at cantonal level) - Who: All residents in Switzerland must obtain coverage - Deadline: Within 3 months of arrival in Switzerland - Deductibles: From CHF 300 to CHF 2500 for adults - Subsidies: Available for those with insufficient income (cantonal criteria)
### The mandatory LAMal system in the Canton of Fribourg
The [LAMal health insurance](nav:health) is mandatory in Switzerland and also valid in Fribourg. It is a private insurance with per capita premiums, not a tax or salary contribution. Anyone who moves to Fribourg or any other Swiss canton must obtain coverage within 3 months of arrival, otherwise they risk administrative penalties. Each insured person pays their own premium, regardless of income or age (except for young adults up to 25 years old, who benefit from flat-rate reductions). Premiums vary depending on the canton of residence, the insurance company chosen, and the insurance model subscribed to (standard, with reduced deductible, HMO models, etc.). In the Canton of Fribourg, like in other cantons, mandatory insurances must cover all residents according to LAMal regulations, without exclusions for pre-existing conditions or health conditions. Health insurance is therefore the cornerstone of Switzerland's national health protection system.
### Deductibles and coverage levels
The deductible is the amount that the insured person pays out of pocket before the insurance begins to reimburse. In Switzerland, deductibles for adults are standardized at the federal level and are available in six levels: CHF 300, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000, and 2500. Those who choose a higher deductible (for example CHF 2500) pay a lower monthly premium; those who choose a low deductible (CHF 300) pay a higher premium. This choice is individual and can be reviewed every year. In the Canton of Fribourg, each resident receives communications from insurance companies with available premiums, allowing them to compare and choose the deductible level that best suits their health profile and budget. In addition to standard deductibles, some insurance models (such as HMO policies or models with mandatory primary care physician) can offer reduced premiums. These models require consulting a primary care physician first before accessing specialists, but allow significant savings on the annual premium. Fribourg canton, like all Swiss cantons, provides subsidies to reduce health insurance premiums for people with low incomes. The subsidies (also called 'premium payment assistance') are determined at the cantonal level according to income, assets, and household composition criteria.
### How premium reduction works in Fribourg
The procedure to obtain the [premium reduction in Canton Fribourg](nav:health) follows the national system: those with insufficient income can apply to the competent cantonal office (generally the social welfare office or equivalent). Criteria vary from canton to canton, but typically include:
- Gross income below a threshold defined by the canton - Limited assets - Household composition (spouse, dependent children)
The amount of the subsidy depends on the gap between the actual premium and the 'payment capacity' calculated by the canton based on income. It is not possible to provide exact amounts without consulting updated data from Canton Fribourg, but the mechanism is transparent: the subsidy partially or fully covers the difference between what the insured person can afford to pay and the actual cost of the premium.
### Deadlines and documentation
Premium reduction applications must usually be submitted by specific deadlines (often coinciding with the year change, in December). Documentation on income (tax return, pay slips, bank statements) and assets must be provided. The decision is notified in writing, and the subsidy is valid for one year, generally requiring renewal every year.
In Canton Fribourg, subsidy management can take place at the cantonal social welfare office. It is advisable to contact the competent office directly to find out the exact forms and deadlines, as these administrative details are subject to annual variations. Subsidies are not automatic: they must be requested every year by submitting updated documentation. Many residents do not know they are entitled to subsidies and continue to pay the full premium; contacting the cantonal welfare office is the first step to verify eligibility. The procedure is generally free and the assessment requires a few weeks.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare [CHF-EUR exchange options](nav:exchange) and [banks for cross-border workers](nav:banks). ### Step-by-step procedure for registration
Step 1: Finding out about available premiums
Within 3 months of arriving in Fribourg (or at the beginning of each calendar year if already resident), gather your identification documents and contact the insurance companies operating in the canton to receive their premium proposals. You can do this online through the insurers' websites or directly at their offices. The offers must include the monthly premium for each available deductible level.
Step 2: Choosing the model and deductible
Assess which deductible level (CHF 300–2,500) and which model (standard, HMO, family doctor model) suits your anticipated medical spending profile. A young, healthy adult might opt for a high deductible and basic model; a person with chronic conditions might prefer a low deductible and broader coverage.
**Step 3: Concluding the contract**
Sign the contract with the chosen insurance company. Coverage will take effect on the 1st of the following month (or from the date you specify, according to the contract). Keep copies of all documents and your policy.
Step 4: Verifying eligibility for subsidies
If your income is low, apply for premium reduction at the social welfare office of Canton Fribourg. Be prepared with your tax return, bank statements, and a copy of your LAMal policy. Renewal deadlines for subsidies are generally in November/December for the following year.
### Useful tools and contacts
To find insurance companies operating in Fribourg and compare premiums, you can use the national comparison tool from the Federal Office of Public Health (FOPH) or directly consult the websites of major insurers. For information about subsidies specific to Canton Fribourg, contact the competent cantonal office (exact name: check on the canton's official website).
It's also useful to use an evaluation tool to estimate your expected annual medical expenses and check what deductible value is most convenient for your situation. [Try our healthcare cost calculator](nav:health) for a personalized assessment.
Remember: LAMal is essential protection in Switzerland. Maintaining continuous coverage avoids penalties and ensures access to healthcare services without unexpected financial risks. Those who fail to obtain health insurance within the required 3 months face a cantonal administrative fine, which can amount to several hundred francs. Additionally, insurance companies can recover costs for healthcare services received during the period without coverage, a significant financial burden. To avoid this situation, take action immediately after moving.

item.title: Opening a business in Zug: trade register and costs
item.description: Canton of Zug: legal forms, federal minimum capital, cantonal registration fees, AVS, LAINF and operational steps to start a business.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Opening a business in Switzerland requires registration in the commercial register of the canton - The choice of legal form determines capital, liability and accounting obligations - Minimum capital and registration fees vary depending on the business form - Insurance and pension obligations commence from the start of the business
## Key Facts - **What**: Starting a business in the Canton of Zugo, with registration in the commercial register - When: Current period - Where: Canton of Zugo, Switzerland - Who: Aspiring entrepreneurs, individuals and legal entities - Amount: Minimum capital according to the chosen legal form (details to be verified with the commercial register office) - Fees: Registration costs determined by the cantonal commercial register office - Insurance: Obligation to have AVS/AI/IPG, AD and LAINF coverage from the first employee
Starting a business in the Canton of Zugo requires a series of mandatory steps that begin with the choice of legal form. This decision determines the amount of minimum capital, the liability regime and accounting obligations. In Switzerland, the most common forms are sole proprietorship, general partnership, limited partnership, joint-stock company (SA) and limited liability company (SAGL).
### The Choice of Legal Form The sole proprietorship is the simplest form: it is registered in the commercial register only if annual turnover exceeds a certain threshold set by law. It does not require minimum capital, but the owner is liable for debts with their own assets. The general partnership and limited partnership involve two or more people, with unlimited liability for the partners.
The SA and SAGL are the most structured forms. The SAGL requires a minimum capital set by law and the SA requires a minimum capital set by law: both amounts are defined at the federal level and apply uniformly throughout Switzerland. The difference between the two cantons therefore cannot concern the minimum capital threshold, but possibly the administrative registration costs.
### Registration at the Zugo Commercial Register Registration in the commercial register is handled by the competent cantonal office. For individuals, registration is mandatory when the business reaches a certain size; for legal entities (SA, SAGL), registration is always mandatory. The procedure includes the submission of the articles of association or partnership agreement, the identification of the founders and the payment of capital.
The registration fees are determined by the commercial register office of the Canton of Zugo and vary depending on the legal form and the complexity of the matter. To get an up-to-date picture, it is advisable to consult the official cantonal website or the competent office directly, as the amounts may be subject to periodic revisions. Opening a business in the Canton of Zug involves a series of practical implications that go beyond simple registration in the commercial register. Swiss taxation is structured at three levels — federal direct tax (FDT), cantonal tax and municipal tax — and each canton has its own tax law and its own multiplier. Municipalities apply an additional multiplier to cantonal tax.
### Taxation and accounting obligations For those starting a business in Zug, the FDT is managed by the Federal Tax Administration (FTA/ESTV), while cantonal and municipal taxes fall under the responsibility of the cantonal tax administration. VAT, when the business reaches the expected thresholds, is also administered by the FTA/ESTV. It is not the task of FSIO/BSV to set tax rates: that federal office is responsible for social security (AVS, AI, LPP).
The choice of legal form affects the tax regime: a sole proprietorship is taxed based on the personal income of the owner, while SA and SAGL are subject to profit tax. In Zug, as in the rest of Switzerland, the municipal multiplier varies from one municipality to another, affecting the overall tax burden.
### Costs and comparisons between legal forms The minimum capital required varies significantly depending on the form chosen. For a sole proprietorship, no minimum capital is required. For an LLC, federal law provides for a specific minimum capital, while for a corporation, the minimum capital is set by federal law at a higher level. These amounts are identical in all cantons and do not change in Zug compared to Zurich, Geneva or Basel.
The fees for registering in the commercial register are, however, under cantonal jurisdiction and can therefore differ from one canton to another. Notary costs, when required for the formation of a corporation or LLC, also vary based on the cantonal fee schedule. For an entrepreneur comparing Zug to other cantons, the main difference lies in the tax rates and municipal multipliers, not in capital requirements.
### Insurance and pension obligations From the moment the business is started and there are employees, a series of contribution obligations are triggered. AVS/AI/DI contributions amount to 10.6% of salary (5.3% borne by the employee and 5.3% borne by the employer). AD/AC contributions are equal to 1.1% up to the annual maximum provided. LAINF/LAA, managed by SUVA for most sectors, ranges from 0.7% to 1.5% of salary depending on the business sector.
If the business is started as an employer, it is necessary to affiliate with the competent AVS compensation fund and take out insurance against occupational and non-occupational accidents. For those operating as self-employed without employees, the obligation to affiliate with a compensation fund remains, with the possibility of choosing the most appropriate contribution class.
### Health insurance and individual obligations The business owner, as a resident of Switzerland, is subject to the obligation to take out health insurance according to LAMal within three months of arrival or when the right arises. Premiums are private, per capita, and do not constitute a salary contribution. Deductibles of the adult's choice start from CHF 300 and reach up to CHF 2500, with intermediate amounts of CHF 500, 1000, 1500 and 2000. Premiums vary by canton and region, and the Canton of Zug provides a premium reduction (subsidy) for low incomes.
From the point of view of rental, anyone who starts a business in Zug and needs commercial premises is subject to the federal provisions of the Code of Obligations (art. 253 et seq. CO): the security deposit cannot exceed three months' rent and must be held in an account in the tenant's name; the landlord's notice is valid only on the official cantonal form; any objection must be filed within thirty days with the conciliation authority.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Step-by-step procedure to open a business in Zug
1. **Define the legal form**. Evaluate the pros and cons of sole proprietorship, joint-stock company, limited liability company or other forms, considering capital, liability and tax regime.
2. Check the need for capital. For joint-stock companies and limited liability companies, the minimum capital is set by federal law; for sole proprietorships, no minimum capital is required. For capital companies, capital must be paid in and deposited before registration.
3. Prepare the articles of incorporation or partnership agreement. The articles of incorporation of a joint-stock company or limited liability company must contain the company name, registered office, purpose, capital and corporate bodies. It can be drafted independently or with the assistance of a notary.
4. Register with the commercial register. Submit the documentation to the commercial register office of the Canton of Zug. Registration fees vary depending on the legal form: for current amounts it is advisable to consult the official website of the canton.
5. Tax registration. Notify the cantonal tax authority of the commencement of business activities and, where applicable, the Federal Tax Administration for federal direct tax and VAT. The VAT declaration must be filed if turnover exceeds the thresholds provided by law.
6. Affiliation with the AVS compensation fund. Mandatory for both employers and self-employed individuals. AVS/AI/IPG contributions start at 5.3% borne by the employee (10.6% total including the employer).
7. Accident insurance (accident insurance law). Take out a policy with SUVA or a recognized private insurer, depending on the sector of activity. The premium varies between 0.7% and 1.5% of salary.
8. Health insurance (health insurance law). The owner and employees must take out coverage within three months. The deductible can be chosen between CHF 300, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000 or 2500.
9. Occupational pension (occupational pension law). If employees are hired with salaries subject to occupational pension law, affiliation with a pension fund is mandatory. Minimum contributions on coordinated salary are 7% (25-34 years), 10% (35-44), 15% (45-54) and 18% (55+ until retirement age).
10. Work permits for foreign citizens. If the entrepreneur is not Swiss, they must verify their permit (L short-term residence, B temporary residence, C permanent residence, G cross-border commuter) with the State Secretariat for Migration (SEM). Starting a business may require a specific authorization depending on the type of permit.
### Subsequent deadlines and obligations After registration, the business is subject to recurring obligations: periodic VAT declaration, declaration of cantonal and federal taxes, payment of pension contributions and submission of annual accounts (for joint-stock companies and limited liability companies). Bookkeeping can be entrusted to an authorized accounting firm.
### Useful tools To get oriented on costs and current tax rates, it is advisable to consult directly the website of the Canton of Zug and that of the Federal Tax Administration. To simulate the impact of taxes and pension contributions on your income, the [salary calculator](nav:calculator) is available, a tool that allows you to estimate the net from the gross and applicable contributions.
For those who want to deepen knowledge on real estate taxation and property taxes, the subject of [tax return](nav:tax-return) is a mandatory step for every new business. Finally, to assess the [cost of living in Switzerland](nav:cost-of-living) — rent, health insurance premiums, transportation — before starting a business in Zug, it is useful to consult the most recent available data.
